title: Democrats Reclaim Control of Congress, Vowing Scrutiny of Trump's Economic Agenda and Corporate Allies
snippet: Democrats flipped key seats to win majorities in both the House and Senate, setting up aggressive oversight of President Trump's economic policies and key allies like Elon Musk.
content:
WASHINGTON — In a major political shift, Democrats retook control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate on Tuesday, dismantling two years of unified Republican rule and drastically altering the environment for President Donald Trump’s economic agenda.

The newly secured majorities hand Democrats significant committee gavels and subpoena power, establishing a fresh platform to launch aggressive investigations into the administration’s key corporate allies, including billionaire Elon Musk, while challenging white-hot policy issues like tariffs and healthcare subsidies.

Broad Oversight: Elon Musk and Wall Street Allies in the Crosshairs

With Representative Hakeem Jeffries poised to assume the House leadership and Senator Elizabeth Warren positioned for an influential role overseeing financial regulation, Democrats are signaling an aggressive oversight posture. Representative Robert Garcia, set to chair the House Oversight Committee, delivered a succinct message to prospective targets: 'Lawyer up.'

Musk, whose defense contracts, oversight role in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), and satellite operations involving Starlink have raised eyebrows among lawmakers, stands near the top of the investigative docket. In response to potential inquiries, Trump suggested he would consider preemptive pardons for allies facing congressional heat.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is likewise bracing for intensified scrutiny over IRS oversight and regulatory rollbacks, setting up high-stakes hearings before Senate and House committees.

Legislative Battles and Bipartisan Openings

Incoming House Budget Committee Chairman Brendan Boyle confirmed plans to challenge the administration's trade tariffs and healthcare cuts. Yet while Democrats hold the gavels, major legislative drives will still encounter structural hurdles, including the Senate's 60-vote filibuster threshold and the threat of presidential vetoes.

Nevertheless, industry experts highlight potential avenues for cross-party collaboration, pointing to shared legislative interests in expanding affordable housing, curbing pharmaceutical costs, and managing the surge of AI data centers.

As Washington transitions to a new power dynamic, market analysts warn that heightened political friction and aggressive regulatory probes could introduce new volatility across key sectors of the US economy.
